name: Cleanroom classification - max total particles per m3 (Table 1)
values: Grade A: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 3520; >=5um not specified (consider if CCS or trends indicate). Grade B: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 352000; >=5um at rest not specified / in operation 2930. Grade C: >=0.5um at rest 352000 / in operation 3520000; >=5um at rest 2930 / in operation 29300. Grade D: >=0.5um at rest 3520000 / in operation not predetermined (site sets from risk assessment and data); >=5um at rest 29300 / in operation not predetermined.

name: Microbial limits during cleanroom qualification (Table 2)
values: Grade A: no growth (air, settle, contact). Grade B: air 10 CFU/m3; settle plate 90mm 5 CFU/4h; contact 55mm 5 CFU/plate. Grade C: air 100; settle 50; contact 25. Grade D: air 200; settle 100; contact 50. Settle plates exposed for the operation and changed after max 4 h (exposure based on recovery studies, no desiccation). All tabulated methods used for a grade unless justified; non-CFU methods need scientifically justified, CFU-correlated limits.

name: Airflow, pressure and clean-up guidance values
values: Differential pressure between adjacent rooms of different grades: >=10 Pa (guidance). UDAF air speed at working position: 0.36-0.54 m/s homogeneous (guidance; other values only if justified in CCS). Clean-up period to return to at-rest particle limits after operations/line clearance: < 20 min (guidance, set in qualification). Settle plate max exposure 4 h per plate.

name: Cleanroom and clean-air equipment requalification maximum intervals
values: Grade A and B areas: max 6 months. Grade C and D areas: max 12 months. Minimum requalification content: total particle classification, final filter integrity, airflow volume, room DP verification, air velocity (risk-based for B/C/D but required for UDAF filling zones e.g. terminally sterilised filling, Grade A background and RABS; recovery test replaces velocity for non-UDAF). Also requalify after remedial action or significant change (air interruption, HVAC/design change, final filter change).

name: Grade assignment examples - terminally sterilised products (Table 3)
values: Grade A (with at least Grade C background): filling when product is unusually at risk. Grade C: solution preparation when unusually at risk; routine filling. Grade D: making up solutions and readying components ahead of filling.

name: Grade assignment examples - aseptic preparation and processing (Table 4)
values: Grade A: aseptic assembly of filling equipment; aseptic connections downstream of the final sterilising filter (SIP preferred); aseptic compounding/mixing; replenishing sterile bulk, containers and closures; removing and cooling unwrapped items from sterilisers; staging/conveying unwrapped sterile primary components on the line; aseptic filling, ampoule sealing, vial closure, transfer of open or part-stoppered vials; lyophiliser loading. Grade B: background to Grade A (non-isolator); protected conveying/staging of items for introduction to Grade A. Grade C: preparation (incl. sampling and dispensing) of solutions that will be filtered. Grade D: equipment cleaning; handling of cleaned components/equipment; assembly of cleaned items under HEPA airflow before sterilisation; assembly of closed sterilised SUS using intrinsic sterile connectors.

name: EM routine monitoring - max total particles per m3 (Table 5)
values: Grade A: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 3520; >=5um at rest 29 / in operation 29. Grade B: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 352000; >=5um at rest 29 / in operation 2930. Grade C: >=0.5um at rest 352000 / in operation 3520000; >=5um at rest 2930 / in operation 29300. Grade D: >=0.5um at rest 3520000 / in operation not predetermined; >=5um at rest 29300 / in operation not predetermined (site sets from risk assessment and routine data). At-rest values to be met after the qualified clean-up period (guidance < 20 min, unmanned). Grade A continuous monitoring sample flow at least 28 L/min (1 ft3/min).

name: Viable particle maximum action limits for routine monitoring (Table 6)
values: Grade A: no growth for all methods (any growth triggers investigation). Grade B: air 10 CFU/m3; settle plate 90mm 5 CFU/4h; contact plate 55mm 5 CFU/plate; glove print (5 fingers, both hands) 5 CFU/glove. Grade C: air 100; settle 50; contact 25; glove print not specified. Grade D: air 200; settle 100; contact 50; glove print not specified. Settle plates in A and B exposed for the whole operation incl. set-up, max 4 h per plate (exposure validated incl. recovery); C and D exposure max 4 h with frequency by QRM; individual plates may be exposed for less than 4 h. Contact limits apply to equipment, room and gown surfaces in A and B; routine gown monitoring not normally required in C and D. Other methods acceptable if they cover the whole critical process; non-CFU methods need justified, CFU-correlated limits.

name: Glossary numeric definitions relevant to eBMR rules
values: Terminal sterilisation SAL: 1e-6 or better. Post-aseptic terminal heat treatment: shown SAL of 1e-6 or better without meeting steam sterilisation requirements (e.g. F0 of at least 8 min). Overkill sterilisation: at least 12 log10 reduction of organisms with minimum D-value of 1 min. Sterilising-grade filter: usually pore size 0.22 um or less. Bacterial retention test: typically Brevundimonas diminuta at least 1e7 CFU/cm2. Dead leg: non-circulating pipe longer than 3 internal pipe diameters. Isokinetic sampling: inlet velocity within about +/-20 percent of local airflow. D-value: duration/dose for 90 percent reduction; Z-value: temperature change for 10-fold D-value change. Equilibration time: from reference point reaching sterilisation temperature to all load points reaching it.

name: Minimum background grade by barrier technology
values: Open isolator: generally at least Grade C (clause 4.20(i)(a)). Closed isolator: at least Grade D. RABS for aseptic processing: at least Grade B. Conventional open aseptic line (Grade A zone): Grade B. Aseptic BFS: machine in at least Grade C with operators in Grade A/B garments. BFS for terminal sterilisation: at least Grade D. Clean-process vial capping under Grade A air supply: background at least Grade D. Terminally sterilised filling: Grade C (Grade A with at least Grade C background when unusually at risk).

name: Personnel and APS frequencies
values: Gowning qualification reassessment: at least annually (visual + microbial: gloved fingers, forearms, chest, hood/mask/forehead). Operator participation in a successful APS: at least once a year. Periodic APS: normally twice a year (about every 6 months) per aseptic process, per filling line, per shift. Initial APS validation: at least 3 consecutive successful runs covering all shifts. After APS failure: normally at least 3 consecutive successful repeat APS. Manual aseptic: each operator 3 consecutive successful APS initially per container/closure/equipment train, then one about every 6 months. APS size: typically at least 5,000-10,000 units; for batches below 5,000 units, at least the production batch size. APS acceptance target: zero growth (any contaminated unit = failure). Visual inspection operator qualification: at least annually incl. eyesight check.

name: Equipment and utility test frequencies and process values
values: Isolator glove integrity test: at least beginning and end of each batch or campaign (session start/end for small manual batches) plus visual check at each use. Steriliser vacuum leak test: periodic, normally weekly. Autoclave air-removal test: normally daily (or air detector). Heat sterilisation revalidation: at least annually for worst-case load patterns. Depyrogenation tunnel HEPA integrity: at least biannually (twice a year). Depyrogenation validation: at least 3 log10 endotoxin reduction with suitable Fh. Liquid sterilising filter: one batch only, not more than one working day continuous use unless validated. Sterilising filter nominal pore size: 0.22 um maximum (also for process gases). Water sampling: at least one representative sample every day of water used in manufacture. WFI storage/circulation example: above 70 C. Particle counter sample tubing: typically no longer than 1 m. Grade A particle sample flow: at least 28 L/min. Lyophiliser leak rate: checked at start of every cycle against specified maximum. Fusion-sealed containers up to 100 ml (glass ampoules, BFS): 100 percent CCI.

name: Validated maximum time windows the eBMR must enforce (values are product/site-specific; Annex 1 requires them to exist)
values: (1) Cleaning-to-drying-to-sterilisation hold of equipment/components/containers [8.18(i)]. (2) Sterilised equipment/components/containers hold before use and during filling/assembly [8.18(ii); 8.46]. (3) Decontaminated RABS/isolator hold before use [8.18(iii)]. (4) Start of product preparation to sterilisation or sterilising filtration, through to end of aseptic filling, per product [8.18(iv); 8.36]. (5) Sterilised product hold before filling [8.18(v)]. (6) Aseptic processing time [8.18(vi)]. (7) Filling time [8.18(vii)]. (8) Terminal sterilisation products: preparation to filling [8.5]. (9) Packing to sterilisation and sterile shelf life of packed items [8.48]. (10) Post-SIP hold under integrity until use [8.63]. (11) Lyophiliser sterilisation to use, as challenged in APS [8.122; 9.33(vii)]. (12) Filtration contact time / maximum filtration time, pre-filtration hold [8.85]. (13) Sterile gown maximum wear time per shift [7.15]. (14) Settle plate exposure max 4 h [9.30]. (15) Clean-up period after operations, guidance under 20 min [4.29]. (16) Disinfectant dilution in-use expiry [4.34; 4.35]. (17) Filter use duration in validated campaigns [8.95]. (18) EO aeration minimum [8.78]. (19) APS unit incubation start without unnecessary delay [9.44].

name: Minimum gowning by grade (summary)
values: Grade B and entry/interventions into Grade A: dedicated undergarments; sterile gloves while donning; sterile headgear enclosing all hair incl. facial hair (tucked into suit); sterile facemask and sterile eye covers enclosing all facial skin; sterilised footwear/over-boots with trousers tucked in; sleeves tucked into a second pair of sterile gloves; fresh sterilised garments at every entry; max wear time from garment qualification. Grade C: hair/beard covered; one- or two-piece trouser suit gathered at wrists with high neck; disinfected shoes/overshoes. Grade D: hair/beard covered; general protective suit; disinfected shoes/overshoes. Extra gloves/facemask in C/D when the CCS identifies a contamination-risk activity. Facility suit and socks worn before entering B and C change rooms.

name: BB-01 Room, zone and line master data (classification and readiness)
purpose: Single source for where each step may run and whether the location is currently fit for use.
fields: grade (A/B/C/D/unclassified) and zone type (Grade A zone vs Grade A air supply)
barrier technology (open/closed isolator, open/closed RABS, conventional, BFS shuttle/rotary)
qualification status and last/next requalification date (A/B 6 months, C/D 12 months)
DP pairs, set points, alarm limits (>=10 Pa guidance between grades) and criticality
UDAF velocity range reference (0.36-0.54 m/s guidance)
cleaning/disinfection status and sporicide due date
rules: Block step start if room/zone grade is below the step's required grade or background grade is below the technology minimum
Block if qualification expired or requalification-required flag set
Block if cleaning/disinfection or sporicide overdue
Start clean-up timer after line clearance/disruption and block restart until elapsed
Raise batch event when occupancy exceeds maximum
Grade A air supply zones excluded from continuous particle and Grade A viable rules but air-supply status recorded

name: BB-02 Personnel qualification gate (sign-on, room entry, e-signature)
purpose: Ensure only currently qualified people perform or sign each activity in each grade.
fields: user ID and roles (operator incl. maintenance/cleaning/EM sampler, inspector, QA, QP, microbiologist)
gowning qualification date and result (visual + microbial), next due (<= 12 months)
APS participation history (line, shift, process, container/closure/equipment train, result, date)
disqualification status and reason (PM trend, failed APS, assessment)
visual inspection qualification + eyesight check date
supervised-entry flag and supervising authorised person
rules: Unsupervised Grade A/B sign-off only with gowning qualified within 12 months AND successful APS within 12 months covering the line/process
Manual aseptic steps require per-operator APS for the specific container/closure/equipment train (3 initial, then ~6-monthly)
Disqualified users blocked from aseptic steps until retraining, gowning requalification and (default) successful APS are linked
Failed APS or PM adverse-trend rule sets disqualification automatically for implicated operators
Unqualified persons may enter only via exceptional supervised-entry record with impact assessment, linked to in-progress batches
Visual inspectors blocked if VI qualification or eyesight check older than 12 months

name: BB-03 Gowning and garment log
purpose: Record each cleanroom entry/exit with garment traceability, checks and wear time.
fields: garment and eye-cover pack lot IDs, sterilisation lot, sterile expiry
gown wear timer vs qualified maximum
glove/garment change events and reason (damage, post-intervention sampling)
exit glove and gown sample IDs (Grade B)
rules: Reject expired, unsterilised or damaged garment packs
Reject garments beyond maximum laundry/sterilisation cycles
Fresh sterile garments required at each Grade A/B entry
Alert at maximum wear time; record as batch event if exceeded
Exit record incomplete until exit integrity check and Grade B exit glove/gown samples recorded
Glove change enforced after post-critical-intervention glove sampling; re-gown enforced after post-intervention gown sampling

name: BB-04 Material and equipment transfer into Grade A/B
purpose: Control and document every item entering or leaving aseptic areas.
fields: approved-transfer-list reference or QA exception ID (risk assessment, disinfection and monitoring plan)
transfer route (double-door autoclave, depyrogenation tunnel, pass-through, airlock, RTP/beta container, bacteria-retentive filter)
outer-layer disinfection: agent, lot, expiry, contact time, operator
packaging layers removed at each grade change
time in / time out and direction (in/out) for time-based separation
non-sterilisable item flag with EM location assignment
rules: Unlisted items blocked unless a pre-approved QA exception is linked
Lower-to-higher grade transfers require a disinfection record
Sterile items require a released sterilisation cycle and valid sterile hold
Where time-based separation is used, overlapping in/out movements raise a warning
Non-sterilisable items added to the batch surface-monitoring plan

name: BB-05 Sterilisation load and cycle record (moist heat, dry heat, EO, contract/irradiation)
purpose: Identify every load and prove each cycle conformed before any item from it is used, and present all contributing cycles at release.
fields: steriliser ID, qualification status, last leak test (weekly), last air-removal test (daily) or air detector result
validated cycle recipe/version and validated load pattern ID (with min/max load)
load contents: item IDs/carriers, product name, batch number, quantity per item type
load carrier labels/electronic tracking state (to sterilise / sterilised-pending review / released / rejected)
control and independent monitoring probe data (IDs, positions), chamber drain temperature, pressure
equilibration time, exposure time, min/max temperature, P-T saturation check, F0 (fluid loads)
dry heat: temperature, exposure time, chamber overpressure incl. hold, air speed/quality, belt speed/dwell and zone temperatures and DP profile for tunnels, Fh
EO: preconditioning time/temperature/RH, gas concentration, pressure, gas amount, RH, temperature, exposure time, aeration start/end, residuals
BI lot (incoming verification status), BI positions, results, positive control
cooling medium and its sterilisation evidence
unload checks: load dryness, per-item damage/packaging integrity/moisture
cycle outcome (automated evaluation) and reviewer approval
contract sterilisation certificate (dose range, processing lot) for externally sterilised items
rules: Only validated recipe + validated load pattern selectable; item counts checked vs min/max
Block steriliser use if leak test, air-removal test, requalification (annual worst-case) or maintenance release is outstanding
Automatic comparison of every critical parameter and phase duration to validated limits; any failure or deviation (incl. longer/shorter phases) quarantines the load and opens an investigation
Exposure timing valid only after full-load equilibration
BI pass can never override a failed physical parameter
Unload dryness and per-item inspection mandatory; unfit items removed and investigated
Items consumable only in 'released' state and within sterile expiry
All cycle IDs contributing to a batch listed in the release package and each must be approved

name: BB-06 Time-window and hold-time engine
purpose: Enforce every validated maximum time in real time from execution timestamps rather than operator arithmetic.
fields: window type (see limit table of 19 windows)
start event and end event references
validated maximum (and minimum where relevant) with validation reference
current elapsed time and projected expiry
rules: Timers start and stop from recorded events (not typed durations)
Pre-expiry warning and hard stop at expiry for sterile holds, prep-to-fill, filtration contact, filling time and aseptic processing time
Expiry mid-operation (e.g. stopper hold during filling) raises an immediate event and requires QA decision
Routine limits cannot exceed the durations challenged in the latest successful APS (holding times, fill duration, lyo sterilisation-to-use)
Exceedances appear in review-by-exception and block certification until dispositioned

name: BB-07 Sterilising filter lifecycle and integrity test record
purpose: Trace every liquid, gas and vent filter and apply the PUPSIT, post-use, redundant and multi-filter logic.
fields: filter serial/lot, part number, pore rating, role (bioburden-reduction prefilter / primary sterilising / redundant / serial-validated train member / critical gas or vent / non-critical vent / lyophiliser integrity filter)
filter sterilisation evidence (autoclave/SIP cycle ID or supplier irradiation certificate)
installation time, batch ID, first product contact time, removal time
use count and sterilisation-cycle count vs maximum; campaign validation reference
PUPSIT: test type (bubble point, diffusion, water intrusion, pressure hold), wetting fluid, temperature, spec, result, instrument ID and calibration, raw data file
post-use test (before removal from housing): same fields
filtration CPPs: volume, flow, upstream/downstream pressure, DP, temperature, time per known volume, total contact time
pre-filtration bioburden sample ID and time
rules: Part number must match the product's MA-registered filter
Serial bound to one batch; continuous use limited to one working day unless validated campaign (then validated maximum enforced)
PUPSIT mandatory between sterilisation and filtration unless an approved waiver is referenced
Post-use test mandatory before removal is recorded; failure blocks certification and opens investigation
Serial-validated multi-filter train: every filter must pass post-use
Redundant train: primary post-use required; on primary failure, redundant post-use test required plus investigation and risk assessment
Critical gas/vent filters: post-use test in housing per batch; results on release checklist
Non-critical vent filters: interval testing, test at installation and before replacement, maximum duration/cycles enforced
Filtration CPP outside validated range triggers deviation
Bioburden sample must precede filtration start (before first filter in redundant set-up)

name: BB-08 Intervention and stoppage log (with intervention catalogue)
purpose: Capture every intervention and stoppage in a structured way that links to APS qualification, EM, sampling and batch disposition.
fields: units removed (count, positions) vs catalogue-defined removal number
post-intervention glove/gown samples and glove change
stoppage cause (auto from PLC where available)
APS in which this intervention was qualified, max frequency demonstrated
rules: Selectable interventions limited to catalogue items qualified by a valid successful APS for the line
Non-qualified intervention requires real-time QA authorisation, auto-deviation and mandatory QA assessment at disposition
Units removed must equal the catalogue number for that intervention/location; APS may never remove more than routine
Critical interventions trigger glove sampling then glove change; gown sampling triggers re-gown
Routine counts per intervention type above APS-demonstrated frequency are flagged
Critical interventions can trigger additional sterility samples (risk rule)
Interventions requiring re-sterilisation (e.g. BFS) block resumption until a passing SIP is linked
All interventions and stoppages shown on the batch timeline with particle/EM data

name: BB-09 Environmental monitoring linkage (viable, total particle, DP, T/RH)
purpose: Bind all environmental data for the batch's rooms and processing window to the batch and evaluate coverage, limits and trends.
fields: EM programme version and generated sampling plan per batch
method (settle plate, active air, contact, swab, continuous particle 0.5/5 um, rapid method)
result, units (CFU or justified non-CFU), limit version in force (alert/action)
continuous particle stream reference (sample flow >= 28 L/min), counter ID and calibration
DP, temperature and RH trends and alarms with acknowledgement and assessment
pre-start, post-disinfection, post-shutdown and end-of-operation samples
rules: Coverage check: Grade A viable and particle monitoring continuous from aseptic set-up/assembly to end of critical processing; gaps flagged
Action limits validated against Annex 1 Tables 5 and 6 maxima; alert levels required (not for Grade A viable)
Grade A any growth = investigation; A/B isolates identified to species
Action excursion links to all batches in the area from sampling until reporting and holds them
Trend rules (consecutive alerts, rising counts, recurring post-maintenance excursions, spore-formers/moulds, flora shifts, repeated low 5 um counts in Grade A) create batch-linked events
Critical DP alarm during open processing requires documented assessment; alarms cannot be silently overridden
Batch cannot be certified while any sample in the window is pending or any linked excursion is open

name: BB-10 Isolator and RABS readiness and integrity
purpose: Prove the barrier system was intact and decontaminated for the batch and capture events that break separation.
fields: glove/sleeve per port: installed date, replacement due (CCS interval), visual check per use
glove integrity/leak test per port at batch or campaign start and end (tester ID, result)
bio-decontamination cycle ID, recipe, agent lot, parameters vs validated ranges, glove-extension confirmation, result
RABS sporicidal disinfection record; RABS glove sterilisation/bio-decontamination per campaign
door opening events (RABS) and glove exposure disinfection records
rules: Block aseptic phase if bio-decontamination failed, was not preceded by cleaning or its hold expired
Block batch start if any glove is past replacement date or isolator leak test overdue
Failed end-of-batch glove test raises a deviation covering the period since the last passing test
RABS door opening requires justification, assessment and glove disinfection before next aseptic step
Glove breach during processing is a batch impact event

name: BB-11 APS status and qualified-envelope engine
purpose: Know at any moment whether a line/process/shift and each operator is covered by a valid APS, and what worst-case envelope that APS qualified.
fields: APS ID, line, process, shift(s), container/closure sizes (bracket/matrix), date, result
initial validation counter (3 consecutive passes) and revalidation due (about 6 months)

qualified envelope: max duration, line speed, max hold times, operators and per-operator time in cleanroom, interventions and frequencies, idle interruptions, campaign length, lyo SIP-to-use interval, filtration-to-lyo time, trays and loading duration, gas used
participants per APS and their roles/interventions performed
status: valid / due / initial validation required / suspended after failure
change-control links that require APS (HVAC, equipment, process, shifts, staffing, major shutdown, new container/closure)
last production date per process (inactivity trigger)
rules: Batch creation/start blocked when line/process/shift APS status is not valid
Routine batch parameters outside the qualified envelope flagged or blocked (configurable)
Approved change tagged 'affects aseptic process' or long inactivity sets 'initial validation required'
Failed APS sets status 'suspended': no production until the required consecutive successful repeat APS (normally 3) are approved
Operator APS currency (12 months; manual aseptic ~6 months per combination) feeds BB-02

name: BB-12 APS batch record
purpose: Execute and document a media fill with the same structure as a commercial batch plus APS-specific reconciliation and failure handling.
fields: master record source/version (commercial) and APS protocol
media/surrogate lots with growth-promotion and sterility status; air replacing inert gas unless anaerobic
units filled, units incubated, units not incubated (with SOP-based justification per intervention), set-up/line-clearance units incubated separately, flush-media units
fill end time, incubation start time, incubation conditions and durations
intervention log (as BB-08) with start/end and persons
EM and PM results for the full APS duration
reading inspectors and their qualification; results per unit; positive controls (reference and local isolates)
rules: Reconciliation must balance with zero unexplained units
Units removed per intervention cannot exceed routine catalogue values
All integral units incl. cosmetic rejects and non-destructive IPC units incubated
Any positive unit = failed APS, triggering BB-11 suspension and BB-13 impact scope (all batches since last successful APS; quarantine of all batches since the failed APS; operator restrictions)
Abort only for reasons that would apply to commercial lots, with investigation

name: BB-13 Batch impact assessment and excursion engine
purpose: Turn any Annex 1-relevant event into a scoped, justified impact assessment linked to every potentially affected batch, and hold certification until resolved.
fields: auto-proposed batch scope (by time window and location)
per-batch inclusion/exclusion decision with mandatory rationale
root cause, product risk statement, CAPA link, residual-risk acceptance
market-impact assessment (for trends affecting released product)
rules: Triggers include: EM/PM action excursion (scope from sampling to reporting) [9.13]; any Grade A growth [9.30]; adverse EM trend [9.11]; failed APS (all batches since last successful APS; quarantine since failure) [9.46]; non-qualified intervention [8.16]; failed or deviating sterilisation cycle [8.41]; failed PUPSIT/post-use/vent filter test [8.87-8.92; 6.19; 8.124]; filtration CPP deviation [8.86]; glove or barrier integrity failure [4.21]; critical DP alarm/air supply failure [4.16]; unplanned maintenance on sterility-critical equipment [5.7]; water action excursion or post-sanitisation results pending [6.12; 6.14]; hold-time exceedance [8.18]; unusual defect rates or critical defect after 100 percent inspection [8.30]; AVI challenge failure [8.32]; lyo leak-rate failure or loss of integrity [8.124]; unqualified person entry [7.5]; sterility test failure [3.2]
Certification blocked while any linked assessment is open
Inclusion/exclusion rationale mandatory for every candidate batch
Assessment outcomes propagate to all listed batches, including released ones where market impact must be considered

name: BB-14 Lyophilisation record
purpose: Treat the lyophilisation chain as an extension of aseptic processing and capture its integrity and loading evidence.
fields: lyophiliser ID, loading mode (manual-open / automated / closed barrier) and CCS sterilisation-frequency reference
last SIP cycle ID, end time, result; hold until loading vs APS-challenged maximum; maintenance/cleaning events since SIP
integrity (vent) filter ID, sterilisation record, integrity test result
start-of-cycle leak rate vs specified maximum; chamber leak test frequency status
trays/rings IDs, sterilisation IDs and inspection status
loading pattern (shelf map, trays, vial counts)
transfer method (conveyor, clean-air cart, portable UDAF, closed boxes) and its Grade A status during transfer; transfer start/end
cycle recipe and key parameters (shelf temperatures, pressures, durations) with alarms
vacuum break gas and its filter
stoppering and stopper seating check at unloading; unseated-stopper handling under Grade A
EM/PM and intervention records for loading/unloading
rules: Manual-open lyophilisers: new successful SIP required before every load (from 25 Aug 2024)
Automated/closed-barrier: SIP interval per CCS enforced
Re-sterilisation required after maintenance or cleaning
Cycle cannot start if leak rate exceeds specified maximum
Vent filter integrity result mandatory for certification
Loading outside the APS-qualified envelope (tray count, loading duration, filtration-to-lyo time, SIP-to-use interval) flagged
Damaged/overdue-inspection trays refused
Sterility samples drawn from each lyophiliser load

name: BB-15 Container closure integrity (CCI) record
purpose: Capture seal-parameter control and integrity testing appropriate to the closure type.
fields: closure type (fusion: glass/plastic ampoule, BFS, FFS, SVP/LVP bag; non-fusion: stopper/crimp, syringe plunger/tip cap)
CCI method (validated; visual inspection not permitted) and equipment ID
100 percent test counts: tested, passed, rejected by reason (fusion <=100 ml)
sampling plan reference and justification (non-fusion or justified reduced sampling >100 ml)
seal parameters (sealing temperatures and uniformity, times, pressures, forming parameters)
vacuum retention test result after predetermined period (vacuum-sealed containers)
mould/tooling ID and change assessment status (BFS/FFS)
rules: Fusion-sealed containers up to 100 ml require 100 percent CCI; master data cannot select sampling
Visual inspection cannot be selected as CCI method
CCI failure opens investigation and blocks certification
Vacuum-sealed containers: certification blocked until vacuum retention result recorded
Seal parameter excursion segregates units produced in the excursion window

name: BB-16 100 percent visual inspection, acceptance sampling and reject reconciliation
purpose: Document individual inspection of every filled unit, defect classification and a closed unit balance for the batch.
fields: inspector IDs with VI qualification and eyesight check validity
inspection rate/throughput, continuous inspection time and breaks
AVI recipe and validation reference; challenge-set ID and results at start and at intervals
inspected, accepted, rejected counts by defect code and criticality (critical/major/minor) from controlled defect library
batch-specific alert limits per defect code (from trend data)
post-inspection acceptance sample (e.g. AQL) results by class
unit reconciliation: units filled, removed at interventions, IPC samples, stopper-height rejects, CCI rejects, VI rejects, QC samples, retained samples, APS/other, good units, unexplained difference
rules: Defect rates above product alert limits open an investigation
Any critical defect found in acceptance sampling of accepted units opens an investigation and blocks release (possible 100 percent inspection failure)
Failed AVI interim challenge puts all units since last passing challenge on hold for re-inspection
Reconciliation must close within configured tolerance; unexplained differences block certification
Defect data stored by code for statistical trending and market-impact assessment on adverse trends

name: BB-17 Capping and crimping record
purpose: Document how stoppered vials stay protected until crimped and that displaced stoppers were removed.
fields: capping mode (aseptic with sterilised caps / clean process under Grade A air supply / manual in isolator or Grade A)
cap lot and sterilisation evidence (aseptic mode)
Grade A air supply status at the capper and background grade (>= D)
stopper-height detection system qualification status, challenge results, reject count
crimp quality checks (e.g. residual seal force if used)
rules: Clean-process capping requires qualified automated stopper-height detection and records its rejects
Loss of Grade A air supply at capping flags affected units
Manual capping only in Grade A locations
Capping rejects included in unit reconciliation

name: BB-18 Bioburden and sterility sampling plan
purpose: Generate and trace worst-case, representative bioburden and sterility samples from execution data.
fields: pre-filtration or pre-terminal-sterilisation bioburden sample: time relative to hold end and filtration/cycle start, location (before first filter if redundant), limit
parametric release: filled-unit bioburden positions and results, organism ID, sterilisation-resistance assessment, endotoxin
sterility samples: start of fill, end of fill, post-critical-intervention samples, cold-spot positions per terminal load (sub-batch), per lyophiliser load
sample origin metadata (unit counter, time, load, position)
rules: Bioburden sample must be taken at the worst-case point and before filtration/sterilisation starts
Each terminal-sterilisation load treated as a sub-batch with its own sterility test
Critical interventions add sterility samples per risk rule
Bioburden result against limit and sterility result are release prerequisites unless an approved short-shelf-life or parametric-release pathway applies
Passing sterility test cannot clear open process nonconformances

name: BB-19 Utilities linkage (WFI, pure steam, process gases, cooling/hydraulics)
purpose: Attach the quality state of every high-risk utility used by the batch at the time of use.
fields: point of use (WFI outlet, pure-steam header, gas drop) per step
WFI loop temperature, flow, TOC, conductivity at use time
daily water sample results for the loop/points used; alert/action status
water system sanitisation events and post-sanitisation chemical / micro / endotoxin result approval status
WFI tank vent filter integrity status
pure steam condensate result and NCG, dryness, superheat test currency
gas lot/CoA or generator status, point-of-use sterilising filter ID and integrity result, periodic gas microbial monitoring status
leak/backflow alarms from hydraulic, heating and cooling systems
rules: Water drawn after a sanitisation is usable only after chemical approval; batches using it are blocked from certification until micro/endotoxin results are approved
Water action excursion links all batches that used the affected point/loop in the relevant period
Steriliser/SIP use flagged if steam quality tests are overdue
Batch-basis gas and vent filter integrity results are release items
Utility alarms in the batch window require assessment

name: BB-20 BFS / FFS process record
purpose: Capture the continuous forming, filling and sealing parameters and integrity controls specific to BFS and FFS.
fields: machine type (BFS shuttle/rotary, FFS single/dual web), background grade
polymer granulate lot / film roll lots with release incl. bioburden/endotoxin
CIP/SIP cycle IDs for product lines and mandrels
extrusion temperature, speed, throat settings; mould temperatures and cooling; forming temperatures/times/pressures; sealing temperatures, uniformity, times, pressures
batch-specific wall-thickness (BFS) and seal strength/uniformity (FFS) test results
parison/support air and product-contact gas filter IDs and integrity status
interventions requiring stop of extrusion/filling and re-sterilisation
rejects by reason (blowing, forming, sealing, cutting)
viable EM coverage from assembly to end of filling
rules: Parameter excursions segregate units by time window
Re-sterilisation interventions block resumption until SIP passes
Mould changes without CCI assessment block batch start
Rejects and sealing issues recorded and investigated per threshold
BFS operators in Grade C must be gowned to Grade A/B

name: BB-21 Single-use and closed system verification
purpose: Verify each SUS/closed assembly from receipt to installation and use, including connections.
fields: part number and approved specification/BOM revision
supplier approval status and sterility-assurance verification
lot/serial, sterilisation proof (irradiation certificate, dose range), certificate of conformance
receipt check and pre-use visual check of outer packaging, pouches and labels
opening method and post-installation visual check (holes, kinks, clamps)
E&L/adsorption assessment status for the product; validated maximum contact time
connection records: method (intrinsic sterile connector type/lot, SIP after connection, open aseptic in Grade A)
pre-use system integrity (pressure decay) test where required
location grade and integrity-at-every-use evidence when outside Grade A
system opening events with follow-up cleaning/disinfection/sterilisation
rules: Lots without sterilisation proof or from unapproved suppliers stay quarantined
Part number mismatch with BOM refused
Open aseptic connections only in Grade A (or subsequently sterilised)
Closed aseptic systems outside Grade A require an integrity result at every use
Operators performing SUS assembly/connections must be covered by an APS including these manipulations

name: BB-22 Equipment status, alarms and maintenance
purpose: Ensure equipment used is qualified, maintained, released and that its alarms and maintenance events are evaluated against the batch.
fields: equipment ID, sterility-critical flag, qualification status/expiry
preventive maintenance due date and return-to-use approval
unplanned maintenance events with sterility impact assessment
in-cleanroom maintenance with follow-up cleaning, disinfection, extra EM and re-sterilisation tasks
alarm events (critical/non-critical) with acknowledgement, evaluation and time
cleaning status, dirty/clean hold expiry, validated cleaning procedure version
rules: Equipment not qualified, overdue for PM or not released after maintenance cannot be used
Critical alarms require immediate documented evaluation before continuation
Unplanned maintenance on sterility-critical equipment requires recorded impact assessment linked to affected batches
In-cleanroom maintenance inserts follow-up tasks that block restart until complete
Equipment sterilisation after reassembly where possible

name: BB-23 Cleanroom cleaning, disinfection and fumigation status
purpose: Keep each room's cleaning/disinfection state current and traceable to validated agents and dilutions.
fields: disinfectant/detergent, lot, sterile status (Grade A/B), expiry
dilution preparation record: time, container status, in-use expiry, microbial monitoring result
rotation of agents with different modes of action; sporicide application date and due date
rules: Grade A/B only sterile disinfectants/detergents (C/D where CCS requires)
Expired dilutions rejected
Disinfection without preceding cleaning flagged
Overdue cleaning or sporicide sets room 'not ready' and blocks steps
Failed fumigation keeps the room unavailable

name: BB-24 QA review and QP certification package (Annex 1 view)
purpose: Present every Annex 1-required element for the batch in one place and prevent certification until all are complete, reviewed and acceptable.
fields: batch header: product, sterility route (terminal / aseptic / aseptic + post-aseptic heat treatment), parametric-release and short-shelf-life flags, CCS version
review-by-exception list: deviations, non-qualified interventions, alarms, hold-time exceedances, parameter excursions, supervised entries, QA exceptions
all sterilisation cycle IDs contributing to the batch with conformity approval
filter test results (PUPSIT or waiver ref, post-use, redundant logic outcome, gas and vent filters, lyophiliser integrity filter)
EM/PM results and trends for all rooms/zones and the whole processing window; pending samples
utility status (water results incl. post-sanitisation approvals, steam, gases)
APS status of the line/process/shift and of each participating operator at time of manufacture
personnel qualification snapshot for all signers
lyophiliser leak rate and SIP status
CCI results, vacuum retention (if applicable), 100 percent inspection results, AQL, reconciliation
bioburden results and sterility results (per sub-batch/load)
linked investigations with batch-scope rationale and status
QP/QA reviewer identity and sterile-manufacturing competence
rules: Certification hard-blocked while any linked investigation is open
Certification blocked if any sterilisation cycle, filter test or vent/gas filter result is missing, failed or unapproved
Certification blocked while EM/PM samples in the processing window are pending, unless an approved short-shelf-life pathway applies (then most recent data reviewed)
Certification blocked while water micro/endotoxin post-sanitisation results for water used are unapproved
Certification blocked if the line APS was failed/suspended at time of manufacture or an APS failure investigation includes the batch
Sterility test pass cannot override any open process nonconformance
EM/trend review signature required

name: BB-25 Master batch record configuration validator (Injectables edition)
purpose: Stop non-compliant recipes at design time so execution-time checks have correct inputs.
fields: product sterility route and justification reference (terminal preferred; aseptic; aseptic + post-aseptic heat treatment)
dosage form and risk flags (supports growth, long hold, non-filterable, ointment/suspension/emulsion, hazardous material, manual aseptic, short shelf life, parametric release)
container/closure type and volume (drives CCI rule), vacuum-sealed flag
per-step required grade and zone type, step type (aseptic / clean / non-classified), CCS critical control point tag and reference
filter train definition and MA-registered filter
validated time windows and limits (with validation references)
intervention catalogue binding and unit-removal numbers
CCS impact assessment for each change
rules: Reject limits looser than Annex 1 minimums (particle and viable tables, requalification and APS intervals) without documented QA justification
Aseptic set-up, connections, filling, lyo loading and open-container transfers must be Grade A steps with qualified background
TS preparation at least Grade D (C when risk flags set); TS filling at least Grade C (A in C when unusual risk)
Fusion-sealed containers up to 100 ml must carry 100 percent CCI; visual inspection not a CCI method; UV not a sterilisation method
Non-filterable products require sterile additions and sterile contact equipment
Master record changes require CCS impact assessment before approval and effectiveness check after

name: BB-26 Terminal sterilisation of filled product (loads as sub-batches)
purpose: Map filled units to steriliser loads and prove each load achieved the validated lethality without damaging containers.
fields: prep-to-fill and fill-to-sterilisation times vs limits
pre-sterilisation bioburden sample (worst case, end of hold) and result
load ID = sub-batch ID, units per load, load pattern, validated reference
cycle data: F0 / temperature-time, equilibration, probe positions correlated to worst-case (slowest heating) positions
superheated-water checks (nozzles, drains) and cooling-water sterility evidence
non-rigid container deformation/leak inspection after cycle
sterility samples from cold-spot positions of each load
parametric release flag and critical-parameter review
post-aseptic terminal heat treatment flag (where used)
rules: Units from a failed or deviating load cannot be released and are segregated by load
Each load tested for sterility separately (unless parametric release authorised)
Filled units not sterilised within the time limit trigger deviation
Deformed/leaking non-rigid containers recorded as rejects in reconciliation

name: Area and zone classification register
purpose: Master data for every room, critical zone, isolator interior and background area: its class, limits and qualification state. Used to check that each step runs in a room of the right class, and to link environmental data to the batch.
fields: zone_type (critical ISO 5 / isolator interior / background / support / unclassified)
rules: Limits default to Table 1 values and can only be changed through change control with a justification
Alert level must always be below action level (glossary definition), otherwise the configuration is rejected
Each MBR step declares a minimum class, and execution in a lower-class zone is blocked
An expired qualification, HEPA certification or velocity check blocks or deviation-gates line clearance
The status in effect at execution time is stored in the batch record

name: Batch environmental window
purpose: Automatically attaches to the batch all environmental and facility data (particles, viable EM, dP, temperature/RH, alarms, power events) for every room and zone the batch used, over the time it was in use.
rules: The window runs from the first to the last aseptic activity in each room, plus a configurable margin
A gap in a data feed is treated as an alarm and needs assessment
Any ISO 5 viable recovery or power event automatically opens a deviation linked to the batch
Every excursion or alarm needs a documented assessment before the section can be signed
QA release is blocked until the section is signed

name: Aseptic personnel roster and qualification gate
purpose: Records every person who entered the aseptic area during the batch (operators, set-up, maintenance, samplers). Checks each person's qualifications at entry and at every signature.
rules: Sign-in and e-signature are refused if gowning qualification is expired or suspended, training is missing, the last media fill is more than 12 months old or did not cover the activity, the person is not authorised, or an exclusion flag is set
The qualification snapshot is stored with every signature
If headcount exceeds the maximum qualified in the media fill, a deviation is raised
The roster is printed or rendered in the executed batch record

name: Personnel monitoring sampler
purpose: Generates and tracks glove and gown surface samples for each aseptic operator, and links their results and follow-up to every batch the operator worked on.
fields: sites (left/right glove fingers, forearm, chest, mask, etc.)
trigger (critical-zone exit / end of session / post-intervention / isolator glove port)
rules: Glove samples are taken at least daily or per lot for every roster member, and gown sites at the configured frequency
High-intervention operators get extra sampling tasks
A glove sanitisation within the configured interval before sampling triggers a warning and needs a justification or re-sample
Batch review is blocked until all personnel monitoring results have come back and been assessed
An action-level result opens an investigation linked to every batch that person worked in the session and sets their requalification status

name: Intervention catalogue
purpose: Master data per line listing every permitted aseptic intervention, with the rules for performing it, documenting it and qualifying it through media fills.
rules: Interventions not in the catalogue can only be recorded through a deviation
Units removed in a media fill may never exceed the number defined for production
Common types must have been simulated in the latest routine media fill, and rare types within their interval
Catalogue changes need QA approval and change control

name: Intervention and stoppage log
purpose: Records every line stoppage and aseptic intervention during execution, with time, duration and detail proportionate to risk. Used to review the batch and to compare it with the media-fill envelope.
rules: PLC or SCADA machine stops are reconciled with log entries, and unmatched stops are flagged for review
Exceeding the catalogue maximum duration, or a clearance-required type, forces a line clearance record before restart
Corrective or major interventions require the extended fields
Each operator's media-fill coverage for the intervention type is checked
Events appear on a timeline with particle and viable data in the review dossier

name: Time-limit rule engine
purpose: Defines, runs and enforces the data-supported time limits for each phase of sterile manufacture (211.111). Timers start and stop automatically from recorded events.
rules: Standard templates: compounding start to filtration start; total filtration time; filtered-bulk hold to fill end; product exposure on the line; sterile equipment, container and closure holds; stopper wash to sterilisation; stopper to crimp; fill to lyophiliser loading; dirty-hold and clean-hold; prefilter use time; fill to terminal sterilisation (terminal configuration)
The MBR cannot be approved while any rule lacks a validation reference
An exceedance blocks downstream steps until a deviation with a justification is approved by QA
A time-limit compliance summary is included in the review dossier

name: Sterilisation and depyrogenation cycle record
purpose: Links each steriliser, oven, tunnel, SIP, EtO or irradiation cycle, with its load, parameters and evidence, to the items and batches it served. Makes sure every load followed a validated load pattern.
fields: actuals (temperature, pressure, time at temperature, F0 or lethality, belt speed, come-up time)
rules: The equipment must be qualified and not overdue for requalification or preventive maintenance, and must have no open change control
The load must match the selected validated pattern, and the recipe must be linked to that pattern
Any parameter outside its validated range fails the load and blocks use of its items
Instruments feeding the record must be in calibration
Come-up time is compared with the validated range and trended
Manual valve steps are completed as an ordered, attributed checklist

name: Sterile item status and genealogy
purpose: Tracks the status and hold-time expiry of every sterilised or depyrogenated item (equipment parts, tools, containers, closures, ready-to-use components) and its path into the batch.
fields: status (dirty / clean / dried / sterile / in use / expired)
rules: Items without a valid sterile status cannot be used in any ISO 5 step
Items past their hold expiry are blocked unless a deviation is approved
Equipment is re-sterilised for every batch unless a validated campaign rule exists
Container and closure lots need a complete preparation record before they are issued to the filler
Ready-to-use items need a CoA, a sterilisation certificate and a current supplier reliability status

name: Filter register and integrity test record
purpose: Tracks each sterilising, clarifying, vent, gas and HEPA filter: its validation fit, usage, integrity tests and link to batches, so a filter failure can be traced to every affected batch.
fields: filter_role (product sterilising / redundant / prefilter / vent / gas / HEPA)
validated_envelope (max dP, flow, temperature, contact time, volume, lots)
post_use_test (type, tester_id, wetting_fluid, temperature, test_pressure, value, product-specific limit, result, printout)
rules: A part number not validated for the product cannot be installed
A filter used once cannot be reused unless validated for reuse, and never beyond the validated number of lots
A passing post-use integrity test is required before filtered bulk is released to filling or the batch goes to review
The integrity-test limit comes from master data and cannot be typed in
A failed test opens a deviation, puts the batch on hold, and links every batch since the filter's last passing test
Vent and gas filters are blocked past their replacement interval

name: Process simulation (media fill) record
purpose: An executed record for each media-fill run, kept separate from commercial batches, that documents conditions, simulated activities, accounting of every unit, incubation and interpretation.
fields: positives (tray / time block, organism to species)
rules: Incubation must stay within 20-35 C and within 2.5 C of target, for at least 14 days in total and at least 7 days per phase with the lower temperature first
The record cannot close as passed until growth promotion has passed and QC has signed as observer
Outcome follows the run-size criteria, and every positive opens an investigation
Invalidation requires an equivalent rule that applies to commercial lots
On closure the line is set to 'post-media-fill clean required'
The record can never be released as product

name: Line aseptic qualification status and envelope
purpose: Holds each line's (and formulation stage's) process-simulation status and qualified operating envelope. Gates batch starts and compares executed batches against the envelope.
fields: envelope (max aseptic duration, max headcount, allowed intervention types and frequencies, line speed range, formats, shift patterns)
pending_triggers (change controls, shutdowns, EM anomalies, sterility positives)
rules: A fill is blocked if the status is not qualified or requalification is overdue
Executed batches outside the envelope raise a deviation at review
A media-fill failure builds the list of impacted batches since the last pass, holds unreleased ones and flags released ones
Returning to qualified status requires the confirmatory runs chosen by the investigation (three consecutive runs if the root cause is inconclusive)

name: EM sampling plan and task generator
purpose: Turns the written EM program into batch-specific sampling tasks per shift, zone and phase, captures execution evidence, and links results and their evaluation to the batch.
fields: method (active air / settle plate / contact plate / swab / particle)
timing (during / end of operation / after decontamination aeration)
rules: Tasks are generated for every shift the batch spans
Critical-surface samples are released only after fill end, and isolator samples only after aeration end
Settle-plate exposure may not exceed the validated maximum
A missed or late sample is a deviation
Each result is evaluated individually (no averaging); an action-level result needs an evaluation, and critical-zone growth needs an investigation
Organism identification is required for ISO 5, adjacent zones and personnel monitoring
Trend rules (frequency over a window, consecutive hits, new flora) link alerts to batches in the window

name: Sterility and endotoxin release evidence
purpose: Makes sure sterility samples represent the whole fill and processing events, and that sterility and endotoxin results are valid, traceable and correctly dispositioned before release.
rules: Release needs every required pull point, plus approved sterility and endotoxin results within specification that are linked to this batch
A positive sets the batch to presumed non-sterile and puts it on hold
A retest is allowed only after an approved invalidation with conclusive evidence of laboratory cause
An inconclusive investigation allows only rejection
Original results are never overwritten
Results must appear in the executed batch record, not only in the LIMS

name: Contamination investigation evidence pack
purpose: A pre-filled, structured investigation for sterility positives, media-fill positives, critical-zone recoveries and personnel-monitoring action levels. Brings together the evidence the guidance expects and proposes the associated batches required by 211.192.
rules: Evidence sections are populated automatically from batch and system data
The investigation cannot close without an assessment of other batches and products
'Lab error' requires attached conclusive evidence, whatever the lab's track record
EM review must include trends beyond the lot's own day or shift
Isolates are compared using the same identification method

name: Sterile batch review dossier
purpose: The Section XII review package: a holistic assessment of how the process and its supporting systems performed for this production run, with signed-off sections, which gates the QA release e-signature.
fields: utility_data (WFI, clean steam, compressed gases, HVAC/HEPA)
rules: The release e-signature is enabled only when every section is signed and no item is open
Exceptions are highlighted (review by exception), but every underlying record stays one click away
Data gaps count as open items
The contents are frozen at release, and later changes to linked sources create a re-review flag
All in-process and laboratory results must be part of the batch record (211.188)

name: Isolator status and glove integrity register
purpose: Isolator-specific state: decontamination validity, pressure integrity, glove/sleeve/half-suit condition and material transfers, with batch impact logic for breaches.
fields: transfer_log (port type, item, decontamination or sterilisation ref)
rules: Aseptic steps are blocked after 'decontamination valid until'
A breach sets 'decontamination required' and opens a deviation, and units filled in the suspect window default to rejection unless QA justifies otherwise
A failed glove test links every batch since that glove last passed
A signed visual check of each port is required before use
The background room must be classified (typically ISO 8)

name: BFS line control record
purpose: Controls specific to blow-fill-seal that sit alongside the general aseptic rules.
fields: ipc (container weight variation, fill weight, leakers, process air pressure)
rules: SIP and extrusion parameters must be within their validated ranges
Overdue machine preventive maintenance or utility integrity checks block the start
Sampling must cover the entire fill
Significant forming or sealing defects open a 211.192 investigation
Final 100% inspection must be able to detect leakers, with its verification recorded

name: Container-closure inspection and unit reconciliation
purpose: Accounts for every unit from filling to good output, including all removals, and records the 100% inspection results that protect container-closure integrity.
rules: A reconciliation outside tolerance needs a deviation
Release requires 100% inspection to be complete
A critical-defect AQL failure blocks the lot and opens a 211.192 investigation
A trend of container-closure integrity defects prompts procedure improvement
Media-fill reconciliation uses the same structure, with the incubation-specific classes

name: Utility and support-system event register
purpose: Links the state of utilities and support systems (WFI, PW, clean steam, process gases, HVAC, power) and shutdown or return-to-service records to the batches they served.
fields: event_type (alarm / OOS / shutdown / power disruption / maintenance / construction)
rules: Aseptic steps may not start while a shutdown event for the room is open without a return-to-service record
Any power disruption that could affect quality automatically creates a batch deviation (211.100, 211.192)
WFI, clean-steam and gas results in the batch window are listed in the review dossier
Events flagged as media-fill triggers set the line's status to requalification pending
